messages:
alex: FYI I'm promoting the runtime-shedder canary from 15% -> 60% at 2026-03-15T16:02:40Z. doing this to validate new batching window.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary rollout initiated by alex at 2026-03-15T16:02:40Z :rocket:

maya: oncall ping — seeing alerts coming in for API 5xx in hosted lane. can you check?

oncall (tia): dropping in. alerts show spike in 502s and 504s, some 500s. sampling traces now.

cs-agent: CS has 3 open tickets right now saying "502 when calling /v1/chat/completions" and one complaining of a 12s timeout. customers flagged high priority.

derek: tracing shows a lot of upstream-reset tcp errors hitting the runtime handler for the canary subset (region: us-west-2, model: starling-v2-quant). p95 latency for canary instances jumped from ~200ms -> 2.5s.

alex: hmm, the shedder flip also enabled the new batching/window heuristic. I thought the default thresholds were safe for starling, but maybe not.

maya: can you confirm if KV cache warmup changed or if batch sizes are larger? both could cause head-of-line and timeouts.

alex: looking — the canary config had batching.window_ms=500 (old was 80ms). That was me. I accidentally left a local test value in the manifest.

oncall (tia): plan: 1) pause rollout 2) revert flag/config for canary 3) add temporary routing to move live traffic off canary 4) notify CS/ops and draft postmortem.

alex: paused rollout. reverted canary flag via config service:
```
curl -X POST https://config.internal/flags/runtime-shedder -H "Authorization: Bearer $CFG" -d '{"env":"canary","value":false}'
```
Waiting for agent sync (~30s).

deploy-bot: [config] runtime-shedder set to false for env=canary by alex at 2026-03-15T16:05:12Z

derek: after config revert, 5xx rate dropped from ~6.1% -> 1.3% in 2 minutes. Still noisy but trending towards baseline. KV cache miss rate is decreasing.

cs-agent: CS posted a message to affected customers and escalated with the support template. Tickets updated.

maya: can we also temporarily route /v1/generate traffic away from canary until everything stabilizes?

derek: applying weighted route rule now:
```
redwoodctl route set --route /v1/generate --scope us-west-2 --weight canary=0 --weight stable=1
```

deploy-bot: [route] routing changed for /v1/generate by derek at 2026-03-15T16:08:30Z

derek: metrics after routing change: 5xx -> 0.4% within 90s, p95 latency returning to ~180ms. KV warmup looks healthy again.

alex: totally my fault — left a dev value. I'll open a PR with stricter pre-rollout validation, and add a canary-only safety check that blocks >20% promotion until KV hit-rate and p95 latency thresholds are met.

maya: please also add a runbook step: if toggling runtime-shedder/batching parameters, run a 2-minute load check on a small traffic slice and validate KV hit-rate and batch sizes.

tia: agree. scheduling an incident follow-up in 30 minutes to capture actions and owners. marking incident mitigated for now, will monitor for 2 hours. reactions :eyes: :white_check_mark:

cs-agent: CS: closed two tickets as "mitigated, please retry", left two customers to confirm. will update if any reopen.

alex: timeline for postmortem: rollout start 16:02:40, alerts ~16:04, config revert 16:05:12, routing change 16:08:30, metrics stable 16:10:00. I'll draft and assign owners for tests, runbook, and guardrails.

derek: recommend a short-term change: disallow batching.window_ms > 200ms in canary profiles unless explicitly approved by runtime-owners. I'll file the config policy PR.

maya: good. once PRs land, add an automated canary gate: require KV hit-rate >= 85% and p95 <= 400ms for first 5 minutes before increasing rollout above 20%.

tia: closing channel for signal-to-noise but staying on monitoring. ping me if anything pops up.

support-bot: customer notifications sent, CS resumed normal queue work.

maya: thanks everyone. lessons learned: double-check local test flags, enforce stricter canary constraints, add short pre-flight load test for runtime-shedder changes.

alex: will get PRs up today and include test harness for batching/window regression. sorry for the churn.

oncall (tia): incident status: mitigated; keep an eye for any resurface. end."
